quickAnswer: Marlborough is a gas-and-apartments city: 58.3% of homes heat with utility gas and only 13.1% with oil, while 44.7% of homes sit in multi-unit buildings (ACS 2022), second highest of 50 towns. National Grid serves the city, so Mass Save heat pump rebates are in play.
body: ## A city where oil barely registers

Marlborough leans on gas, not oil. According to the Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS), oil or kerosene heats 2,160 of 16,524 occupied homes, just 13.1%, against 36.5% for the middle town and 49th place out of 50. Utility gas heats 9,627 homes (58.3%), electricity 3,994 (24.2%, fourth highest) and bottled gas 509 (3.1%).

Gas equipment is the biggest group by far, so many decisions here are repair or replace rather than a choice of fuel. The oil households are a minority, and for them a gas conversion is a realistic option when a main runs past the house. The 24.2% of homes on electric heat are the other group worth a second look, since a heat pump can heat and cool from one system.
## Second in the state for apartments, condos and duplexes

Marlborough ranks second of the 50 towns for homes in multi-unit buildings: 7,777 of 17,416 housing units, or 44.7%, compared with 16.1% in the middle town. Detached single-family houses are 7,757 units (44.5%), which puts the city 49th for that type. Buildings of five or more units hold 4,842 homes (27.8%), two-family houses hold 1,676 (9.6%), and buildings of 3 or 4 units hold 1,259 (7.2%). Attached townhouse-style units add 1,414 (8.1%).

One more category is easy to overlook: 468 mobile homes (2.7%). Those homes often have compact, factory-built heating systems and limited space for equipment, so replacement is a fitting exercise as much as a sizing one.

Renters live in 7,048 households, 42.7% of the city and ranked 3rd among our towns. For owners of rental buildings, a boiler that fails in January is a safety issue. Under 105 CMR 410.201 the minimum is 68 F between 7 a.m. and 11 p.m., and 64 F overnight, for as long as the heating season runs, roughly mid-September to mid-June. Unless the lease says otherwise, the landlord pays for that heat. That is general information, not legal advice.
## Shoes, streetcars and the pre-1940 housing

Samuel Boyd and his brother Joseph opened the first shoe manufacturing business in 1836, and by 1890, with a population of 14,000, Marlborough was a major shoe manufacturing center. It was incorporated as a city that year. Marlborough is also believed to have been the first community in the country to get a charter for a streetcar system. Today 3,758 units (21.6%) date from 1939 or earlier, 12th highest of the 50.

Later waves built the rest. Another 4,971 units (28.5%) went up from 1960 to 1979 and 4,743 (27.2%) between 1980 and 1999, and the median home dates to 1972. Since 2010 the city has added 1,130 homes (6.5%). So 60.0% of the stock predates 1980, close to the 57.2% of the middle town, but spread across very different construction eras. Buildings from different eras can need very different systems, and no single replacement plan fits them all.
## Highways, office parks and the lakes

Interstate 495, U.S. Route 20 and Route 85 cross the city, Interstate 290 ends there, and the Massachusetts Turnpike helped turn a shoe town into a high-technology one. The Southwest Quadrant, near Interstate 495, is filled with office parks and corporate buildings, and the Marlborough Center Historic District along Main Street holds restaurants, salons and shops. Those are commercial heating and cooling jobs we take on alongside residential work. Lake Williams, Millham Reservoir and Fort Meadow Reservoir all lie within city limits.
## National Grid and the rebates

The city is on National Grid's official Massachusetts Electric Company territory list. That puts Marlborough owners on the Mass Save track for heat pump rebates, and the [heat pump page](/cities/marlborough/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) shows how the city's housing mix lines up with them.

| Marlborough, MA at a glance (ACS 2022) | Figure |
| --- | --- |
| Population | 41,391 |
| Housing units | 17,416 |
| Median year homes were built | 1972 |
| Homes in multi-unit buildings | 44.7% |
| Renter households | 42.7% |
| Homes heated with utility gas / fuel oil | 58.3% / 13.1% |
| Electric utility | National Grid |

faq.q: Is natural gas the norm in Marlborough?
faq.a: Yes. Utility gas heats 58.3% of occupied Marlborough homes, and oil only 13.1%. If you do burn oil, ask whether a gas main runs past your house, since conversion may be an option. A heat pump is another route, and we compare the choices at the estimate.

faq.q: Marlborough has a lot of apartments. Who fixes the heat in a rental?
faq.a: The landlord, unless the lease says otherwise. With 42.7% of households renting, third highest of the 50 towns, tenants should report an outage in writing and keep a copy. The state minimums are in the city story above. This is general information, not legal advice.

faq.q: Do Marlborough homeowners qualify for Mass Save heat pump rebates?
faq.a: Generally yes, since National Grid serves the city. The rebate depends on the weatherization of the house and on the installer, and the amounts can change. The heat pump page sets out what the city's housing mix means for that, and masssave.com has the current terms.

faq.q: Do you work on offices and shops in Marlborough, or only homes?
faq.a: Both. The Southwest Quadrant near Interstate 495 is filled with office parks and corporate buildings, and the Main Street historic district holds restaurants, salons and shops. Businesses and building managers can phone (508) 786-8755, including for emergencies outside office hours.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Utility gas heats 58.3% of Marlborough homes, so gas boilers and furnaces are the main equipment here. The job usually turns on venting, permits and, in shared buildings, keeping tenants warm.
body: ## Gas first, in buildings of every size

Utility gas heats 9,627 occupied homes in Marlborough, which makes a gas boiler or furnace swap the most common replacement decision in the city. The paperwork matters as much as the unit. A licensed plumber or gas fitter pulls the permit for a new gas appliance, an inspection follows the install, and the venting and combustion air are checked along with the equipment.
### Condos, duplexes and larger buildings

Some 44.7% of the city's homes share a building with others, and where one boiler serves more than one household, we plan the work around the days the building can be without heat. Boilers in older multi-family buildings can need careful piping and a pressure test.
### Older buildings

A boiler job in a building that dates to 1939 or earlier, and 3,758 units do, usually means radiators, deep basements and chimneys. That is a piping and flue exercise, quite unlike a furnace swap in a newer condo. We look at the radiators, the pipe runs and the chimney before we suggest a size.
### Mobile homes

Marlborough has 468 mobile homes. Their heating equipment is often compact and made for a specific space, so replacement depends on matching the unit to the available room, venting and fuel. We measure first.
### Beyond gas

About one home in eight burns oil (2,160 homes), and 3,994 use electricity. At replacement, the oil home weighs a new oil boiler against a gas conversion, if a main reaches the street, or a heat pump. Ask what the conversion would cost before you decide, since it can vary from street to street. Electric-heat owners can start with the [heat pump page](/cities/marlborough/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### Landlords in January

With 7,048 renter households, plenty of Marlborough boilers belong to landlords who need them running through a cold week. A written estimate lets the owner weigh repair against replacement before the building goes cold.
### Repair or replace

A cracked heat exchanger, a failing boiler section or a repair bill that keeps growing points to replacement. One failed part on a younger system is a repair. We say which one you have before work begins.
### No-heat calls
Phone (508) 786-8755. Emergency calls are taken around the clock.

faq.q: How long does a gas boiler replacement take?
faq.a: That depends on the piping, the venting and the size of the building, so no honest number can be given before someone has seen the system. What we can do is walk the job, list the steps in the written estimate and flag anything that needs a permit or an inspection.

faq.q: Can I convert from oil to gas in Marlborough?
faq.a: Often, if a main runs past your house and the utility can connect you. Only about 13.1% of the city's homes burn oil, so gas mains are common, but cost varies by street. A heat pump is another option, and we compare the routes in the estimate.

faq.q: My Marlborough condo building has one boiler. Who decides on replacement?
faq.a: Usually the owners' association or the building's manager, since the boiler serves every unit. With 44.7% of the city's homes in multi-unit buildings, shared systems are common here. Records of past service help the board plan, and we can walk the board through repair and replacement options.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: With 44.7% of Marlborough's housing in multi-unit buildings and 44.5% detached, cooling can be as much about apartments, condos and townhouses as houses, and outdoor unit placement often decides the project.
body: ## Cooling when so many homes share a wall

Marlborough ranks near the bottom of our list for detached houses and near the top for multi-unit buildings. In shared buildings the question is not one central system for one house but where the outdoor equipment can go, who owns the wall it sits on, and whether each unit gets its own system.
### Condos and townhouses

In an attached home, equipment space is tight. Outdoor condensers need clearance and a stable pad, and some associations restrict where they can sit. We confirm the rules and the layout first, then recommend a split system or a ductless one. The [heat pump page](/cities/marlborough/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) covers units that both cool and heat.
### Apartments

In older buildings with radiators and no ducts, ductless mini-splits avoid opening walls. In a rental, one system per apartment keeps each household's cooling separate from the next, if the landlord agrees to the equipment and its placement.
### Older and newer homes

The city has pre-1940 buildings and homes from the 1980s and 1990s, and they cool differently. Older houses often have little duct space, while newer houses are more likely to have ducts that can take a cooling coil. Many older homes were built without central air.
### The newest stock

Some 2,232 of the city's units date from 2000 or later (12.8%), and 1,130 from 2010 on. Younger buildings tend to be tighter and may have ducted systems that were laid out with cooling in mind, so a coil swap or a heat pump condenser upgrade is often the question there. The median home overall dates to 1972.
### Office and commercial space

The office parks near Interstate 495 and the shops downtown carry their own cooling loads. We service businesses as well as homes, and a commercial job starts with the same questions about load and equipment placement.
### Diagnosis and sizing

Before replacement we check what is actually wrong, since a weak part is not always a dead system. When replacement does make sense, we size it from the building, including windows, insulation and orientation, so it does not short-cycle.
### Electricity and heat
Electricity already heats 3,994 Marlborough homes (24.2%), fourth highest of the 50 towns. For those households a heat pump can do the cooling job and the heating job from one set of equipment.

faq.q: Can I put an outdoor AC unit on my condo?
faq.a: It depends on your association's rules and the layout. We check clearance, drainage and the electrical supply, then propose a placement the association can approve.

faq.q: What is the best cooling option for an old apartment with radiators?
faq.a: Often a ductless mini-split, because it needs no ducts and only a small wall opening. The number of indoor heads depends on how many rooms need cooling and how the apartment is laid out.

faq.q: Does it matter that Marlborough has so few detached homes?
faq.a: It does. Detached houses are 44.5% of units, and attached or multi-unit homes make up the rest. In shared buildings, the owner or association often sets the rules for outdoor equipment, so approval usually comes before design.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Marlborough is a National Grid city, and 3,994 of its homes (24.2%) already heat with electricity, fourth highest of 50. Only 12.8% of its housing dates from 2000 or later, so most owners meet the weatherization step before any heat pump.
body: ## Heat pumps in a gas-and-apartments city

National Grid serves Marlborough, so the Mass Save whole-home rebate of $2,650 per ton, up to $8,500 per home, is the figure to start from, provided the house has been weatherized first. The full terms are on our [main heat pump page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### What the fuel counts say

Gas heats 9,627 homes, electricity 3,994, oil 2,160 and bottled gas 509. For the electric group a heat pump usually replaces resistance heat. For the oil and bottled-gas homes it can take over the work of a fuel that arrives by delivery. For the gas majority, the usual role is a second system that adds cooling and carries the milder months, and the partial-home rebate track exists for that case.
### The weatherization question

Units from 2000 or later total 2,232 (12.8%), which is the group that clears the age test on its own. The 4,743 units from 1980 to 1999 (27.2%) do not, and neither do the 10,441 built before 1980 (60.0%). In practice, most owners should expect a Home Energy Assessment to be the first step.
### Housing types that need ductless
- Two-family houses: 1,676 units, where one outdoor unit per floor is a common layout.
- Buildings of 3 or 4 units: 1,259 units.
- Buildings of five or more: 4,842 units (27.8%), where outdoor-unit placement needs approval first.
- Townhouse-style attached units: 1,414.
- Mobile homes: 468, where space for equipment is limited.
A ductless system can serve one apartment or a converted attic without touching the rest of the building. In a condo, the outdoor unit location is the first design question.
### Gas homes

Add a heat pump alongside the furnace and the furnace keeps handling the coldest days, while the heat pump covers summer cooling and much of the shoulder season. We size both parts from one load assessment so they do not fight each other.
### Older apartments

Radiator buildings from 1939 or earlier (3,758 units, 21.6%) have no ducts to reuse. Ductless heads or a small ducted unit in a closet are the usual routes, and the building's owner has to be part of the decision.

faq.q: Does a heat pump make sense in a gas-heated Marlborough home?
faq.a: It can, mainly to add cooling or to cut how often the furnace runs. Utility gas heats 58.3% of homes here, so most of the city sits in this group. A partial-home setup keeps the gas system for the coldest days, and we size both parts from one load assessment.

faq.q: Is my Marlborough condo eligible for a rebate?
faq.a: Possibly. It turns on the electric account, the installer and the weatherization condition, and the association may need to approve outdoor equipment. About 44.7% of the city's homes share a building, so ask the association early about where an outdoor unit may go.

faq.q: Do heat pumps work through Massachusetts winters?
faq.a: Cold-climate models are built for them. In a house that is tight and correctly sized, a heat pump can carry most of the heating season. In a leakier house, it may be paired with the old furnace or boiler for the coldest nights.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: In a gas-heated, apartment-heavy city, tune-ups protect shared boilers and keep gas equipment safe. A pre-October visit is a good way to head off a cold-night call.
body: ## Tune-ups for a gas city

Most Marlborough homes burn utility gas, so most tune-ups are safety and efficiency inspections: burner, heat exchanger, venting, controls, and carbon monoxide readings. The 2,160 oil households need the burner cleaning that oil systems call for each year, and electric and heat pump homes need coil, filter and refrigerant checks.
### Property owners with tenants

Over 40% of households rent. If you own a duplex or a larger building, one boiler failure can leave several households cold. A service call before the heating season finds worn igniters, weeping valves and failing pumps while the weather is still mild.
### Condo boards
Shared systems in condo buildings suit a regular service schedule, and the records help when the board plans a replacement.
### Seasonal calendar
- **Early fall:** boiler and furnace service.
- **Late spring:** cooling and mini-split checks.
- **Anytime:** call about noises, smells, short cycling or odd bills.
### Older buildings
Buildings from the shoe-factory era may carry older radiators, valves and chimneys. A yearly inspection finds leaks and corrosion before they become emergencies.
### Systems from the 1980s and 1990s

Marlborough has 4,743 units from 1980 to 1999 (27.2%). Equipment installed in the first decades after those homes were built can now be at the age where parts begin to wear. A check lets you plan a replacement before a failure plans it for you.
### Between visits
Change filters, keep clearance around the equipment, keep outdoor units clear of leaves and snow, and test your smoke and carbon monoxide detectors.
### Mobile homes
The city has 468 mobile homes. Their equipment sits in tight spaces, so filter changes and venting checks matter, and access is part of the planning.
### What a visit includes

A tune-up generally covers the burner or compressor, the thermostat, the condensate drain, the electrical connections and the filter. The technician should explain what was found and note any part that is wearing out. If a repair turns up, the estimate comes in writing before any work starts, and a clean report is a perfectly good outcome.
### When to book
Demand for heating service tends to rise in the first cold weeks, and for cooling service in the first heat wave. Booking ahead of either gives you more choice of days.

faq.q: How often should a gas boiler be serviced in Marlborough?
faq.a: One visit a year, scheduled before the first cold weeks. The technician checks combustion, venting and the safety controls. With utility gas heating 58.3% of homes in the city, this is the usual maintenance call, and it is also a good time to ask about the age of the boiler.

faq.q: Is a service agreement worth it for a rental building?
faq.a: A yearly pre-season visit is a good habit for any building where several households depend on one system. Ask what is covered before you agree. Marlborough has 7,048 renter households, so many boilers here serve tenants, not owners.

faq.q: Do oil-heated Marlborough homes need a different visit?
faq.a: Yes. An oil burner needs cleaning, a nozzle and filter change and a combustion check, while a gas unit is inspected instead. About 13.1% of the city's homes burn oil, so this is the smaller group, but the visit is longer.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Marlborough's housing runs from pre-1940 buildings to homes built since 2010. Shared walls, damp ground near water and gas appliances can all affect air quality, so we start with the building, not the product.
body: ## Air in shared buildings and old floors

Indoor air in Marlborough varies with the building. Buildings of different ages and types hold air differently. The first job is to understand how air moves and where moisture and pollutants come from.
### Shared walls and hallways

In multi-unit buildings, air travels through shared walls, floors, hallways and chases. Cooking odors, smoke and cleaning products can pass between units. Air sealing between apartments, working exhaust fans and sound ductwork reduce it. With 7,777 units in multi-unit buildings, this is the typical Marlborough case.
### Gas appliances

Because gas is the main heating fuel, combustion safety is part of air quality: properly vented equipment, carbon monoxide detectors, and range hoods that exhaust outdoors. A technician can check venting during a tune-up.
### Water on three sides of the map

Lake Williams, Millham Reservoir and Fort Meadow Reservoir sit inside the city. A basement that smells musty is a moisture question, and a dehumidifier treats the air while the source stays untouched.
### Older and newer construction

Older homes tend to leak, which dilutes some pollutants and admits dust and pollen. Newer ones are tighter and need ventilation so moisture and fumes do not build up. Marlborough has 2,232 units from 2000 or later (12.8%), and that is where ventilation can matter most. In compact spaces such as mobile homes, a bath fan and a range hood that vents outdoors can help, because moisture has little room to disperse.
### Four age bands, four starting points

The city holds 3,758 units from 1939 or earlier, 1,712 from 1940 to 1959, 4,971 from 1960 to 1979 and 4,743 from 1980 to 1999. A building from the earliest band and one from the 1980 to 1999 band do not breathe the same way, so the fix starts with the building, not the product catalog.
### Filters and ducts
Better filtration helps when the blower can handle the airflow. Ducts should be cleaned only if they are visibly dirty, moldy or damaged.
### What we can set up
- Higher-grade filtration with a change schedule.
- Humidity control with a dehumidifier or humidifier.
- Ventilation for tight homes.
See our [maintenance page](/cities/marlborough/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups) for how filters and checks fit the year.

faq.q: Should I clean my air ducts?
faq.a: Not automatically. Look first, and if you cannot see dirt, mold or damage, there is little to gain. We inspect first and tell you plainly whether cleaning would help.

faq.q: Can a carbon monoxide detector replace a tune-up?
faq.a: No. A detector warns you of a problem. A tune-up finds the venting or combustion fault before it becomes one.

faq.q: I rent an apartment in Marlborough. What can I do about stale or smelly air?
faq.a: Run the bath and kitchen fans, keep a window cracked when cooking, and use a portable filter. For anything in the ductwork or shared ventilation, the landlord has to act. About 42.7% of the city's households rent, so this is a common situation.
